title: Bebe Ridgely, Zoo Robertson, Roy Palmer and Frankie Dusen
summary: Morris answers about trombonists and cornetists Ridgely, Zoo, Palmer and Oliver's band, and says Dusen worked with everyone and ran the Pelican place.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Some place there now on Tulane and Ramport. Yeah, he got his leg cut off now.
Do you remember Bebe Ridgely on trombone?
Yeah, I remember Bebe Ridgely. That's when they put the pelican up. Bebe Ridgely had that over in charge, when the pelican used to be there. He used to play that.
Another trombonist, did you ever hear Zoo Robertson?
He left here pretty early. He might have left before you came up.
Yeah, well I know Zoo used to play cornet when I used to play in the Silver Leaf, man.
Yeah, he was a cornet player, the one I know. He was a youngster unto me though.
He was younger than you? No, this fellow would be, he wasn't very old, but still he would have been a few years older than you.
Roy Palmer, did you ever hear him play? He went to Chicago very early, Roy Palmer. He was the pupil of Jim Humphrey too.
Yeah. Roy Palmer. But I used to heard your talk of Roy, but I didn't know him. Didn't know him?
No. He went up with Lawrence Dilley and Sugar Johnny.
Those scholars. Who worked in Joe Oliver's band? Do you remember any of those guys?
In Joe Oliver's? No. I don't remember none of them used to work in Joe Oliver's band.
Remember any of the guys with Cap'n?

No, not him either. Because they left you right behind one another. Oh, I see. Yeah. But I mostly believe Frankie Duesen worked with all of them, him. Oh, yeah. Frankie Duesen, he just was the fellow you know. He used to get all them jobs and get who he wants. See, on the counter, that Pelican, well that was Frankie Duesen's place there, that Pelican place there. That was his place.
